title: Route handlers and backend-for-frontend patterns
description: Build API endpoints inside the App Router using Route Handlers and the backend-for-frontend pattern.

data.text: In the App Router, **Route Handlers** replace API Routes from the Pages Router. They live in `app/api/` and use standard Web `Request` and `Response` objects. This makes them closer to frontend developers and easier to test in isolation.

A **backend for frontend (BFF)** is an API layer shaped specifically for one client. Instead of exposing every database table to the mobile app, you build a thin route handler that knows exactly what the UI needs: the right shape, the right permissions, and the right error format.

items: You receive a `Request` object and return a `Response`.
They run on the server by default, so you can import database clients safely.

data.title: Mental model
data.text: Think of Route Handlers as tiny serverless functions. They are isolated, cacheable by default, and can be deployed to Node.js or Edge runtimes depending on your configuration.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Route Handlers are first-class API endpoints in the App Router.
They use standard Web Request and Response objects.
Use them as thin BFFs that shape data exactly for your UI.
data.takeaway: Route Handlers let you keep backend logic inside your Next.js app without a separate API server.
